headline: Going Commando joins the prebuilt games, with no compiler needed
summary: Going Commando's USA v1.01, PAL and USA v2.00 releases now come prebuilt on the launcher's Development line, so players need only their ISO instead of a compiler and local build (#511). Windows source builds can install missing development tools automatically (#514). Texture-pack stutter fixes also landed, with #526 reporting shorter frames and faster Novalis loading, followed by a Linux and Linux arm64 compilation fix (#528). The separate prerelease v1.0.3-dev.956 was published for the prebuilt-game work.
highlights: Going Commando restores Press START, pause, weapon sounds and level AI (#532), fixes Aranos' hatch opening too early (#533), and adds touch Retry and Quit buttons in minigames (#524).
Ratchet & Clank's raised Hoven pool now lifts its visible water, tested on Windows PAL v2.00 (#515). Visibomb signal-loss static now covers widescreen views (#516).
FSR gets steadier scenery motion and enhanced rendering caps its effective scale at 100%, keeping the saved preference (#517). Offscreen Going Commando scenery keeps casting shadows (#530).

SDK interface 1.16 keeps mod data with game saves (#487), and 1.17 adds the game's collision queries (#489). Ratchet & Clank gets weapon-target hooks (#464). Refused mods have their callbacks cleared before unloading (#476).

The launcher keeps header buttons visible during tab changes (#519), scrolls crowded top bars and contains long Settings paths (#529). Configure repairs stale decomp paths and missing submodules (#531).
Texture and held-weapon exports (#518) and revised distant-object activity (#534) opened as drafts. Gadgetron icon customization (#535) is also proposed. None of these three merged.
